questions.e: "Àkọlé" (title or heading) is the standard, commonly used word here. The other options are less common or uncommon forms. This tests recognising correct Yoruba vocabulary.
questions.s: Kínní ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó jọjú nínú wọ̀nyí?

questions.e: "Ọkọ̀ ayọ́kẹ́lẹ́" (motor car) is a compound noun made by joining words together, unlike the simple single nouns odò and ọkọ.
questions.s: Kínní apẹẹrẹ ọ̀rọ̀ orúkọ tí a fọwọ́ jẹ?

questions.e: An atúmọ̀ is the person or device that translates words from one language to another. Ìtúmọ̀ is the translation itself, not the translator.
questions.s: Èrọ tí a fi túmọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ kúrò ní èdè kan sí èkejì ni ...?

questions.e: In "Mo jẹ àkàrà lọ́jọ́ yẹn", "jẹ" (ate) is the verb, the action word at the head of the predicate (àsọyé) that tells what the subject "Mo" did. It is not a noun or an example. The correct option is A.
questions.s: Kínní ipa ọ̀rọ̀ "jẹ" nínú gbolohun Mo jẹ àkara lọ́jọ́ yẹn?

questions.e: "Bí i pé" (as if) introduces a comparison between the rain and the sky collapsing, so it is the comparison or simile marker in the sentence.
questions.s: Kí ni ọ̀rọ̀ àpẹẹrẹ nínú gbolohun: Òjò ń rọ bí i pé ọ̀run ń șú?

questions.e: "Sí" in "sí orí tábìlì" points to where the gift was placed, so it works as a preposition (ọ̀rọ̀ atọ́kùn), the function the option calls ọ̀rọ̀ amúlò.
questions.s: Kí ni ipa ọ̀rọ̀ "sí" nínú gbolohun Ó fi èbùn náà fún mi sí orí tabili?

questions.e: This item tests spotting a function word in a sentence. In "Bí mo ṣe jí", "ṣe" works with "bí" to mean "as/when I woke". The grammatical label in the question is loosely worded.
questions.s: Kínní ọ̀rọ̀ ìfarapa nínú gbolohun Bí mo șe jí, mo rí pe mo ti rẹ̀?

questions.e: Proverbs (òwe) are a marked feature of good Yoruba letter writing, adding wisdom and style to the message. Grammar and joining sentences are general features of any letter.
questions.s: Kí ló jẹ́ afihan-an lẹ́tà àtọ́ka?

questions.e: A command sentence (gbólóhùn àṣẹ) gives an order or instruction, as "Kó lọ ra àkàrà" does. "Ó ra àkàrà" is a statement, and the other two options are questions. The correct option is A.
questions.s: Kínní àpẹẹrẹ gbolohun àșẹ?

questions.e: In "Ó yára gba ìpè náà", "yára" describes how the call was taken, meaning quickly (ní kíákíá). It is not a noun for a room, despite looking like "yàrá".
questions.s: "Yára" nínú gbolohun "Ó yára gba ipe na a" túmọ̀ sí ...?

questions.e: "N" (ń) in "Mo ń lọ sí ilé" marks continuous or progressive aspect, showing the action is happening now, so it is a tense or aspect marker (àmì àsìkò).
questions.s: Kínní ipa ọ̀rọ̀ "n" nínú gbolohun Mo n lọ sí ilé?

questions.e: "Ó ra aṣọ tuntun" (he/she bought new clothes) simply states a fact, so it is a statement or declarative sentence. It is not a question or a command.
questions.s: "Ó ra așo tuntun" jé apeere gbolohun ...?

questions.e: A proverb (òwe) is a saying of wisdom (ọ̀rọ̀ ọgbọ́n) handed down from the ancestors and used to make a point briefly and wisely.
questions.s: Òwe jé ...?

questions.e: Ìkọ ọmọ is a Yoruba ceremony connected with a child, usually tied to the naming period, so it is the child-related celebration. Ìkórè is a harvest festival, not a child's rite.
questions.s: Àșà ayęyę omọde ní ...?

questions.e: "Sáló" means to run away or flee, especially to escape danger, which matches "sá àsálà". "Kó lọ" (pack and go) and "bọ̀" (come) do not carry the idea of fleeing.
questions.s: Kínní ìtumọ̀ "sáló"?

questions.e: Yoruba poetic songs are used mainly to teach, guide and advise listeners, so their key aim is instruction (ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́), not mockery, play or competition.
questions.s: Kí ni àfojúsùn orin ewì to pataki?

questions.e: "Alágbẹ̀dẹ lásán kì í fi àgùnbánirọ̀ sùn" is a short, fixed traditional saying carrying wisdom, which makes it a proverb (òwe), not a praise poem or religious text.
questions.s: Alágbẹ̀dę lásán kì í fi àgùnbánirọ̀ sùn jẹ́ ...?

questions.e: Ìsọmọlórúkọ, the naming ceremony, is the Yoruba celebration held for a newborn, when the baby is formally given names, usually on the eighth day for a boy and the seventh for a girl.
questions.s: Àșà Ayeye omọ tuntun ni ...?

questions.e: "Ìpalára" means harm or injury, so its closest meaning is ìfarapa (getting hurt). Ẹ̀sùn means accusation and àìlera means illness, which are different ideas.
questions.s: "Ìpalára" túmò sí ...?

questions.e: Ìjálá is the chanted poetry of hunters (ọdẹ), traditionally linked to Ògún. They use it to praise heroes, animals and their craft.
questions.s: Àwọn tó máa ń kọ orin ìjálá ni ...?

questions.e: Oríkì (praise names or lineage praise) identifies a child's family line and origin, so it marks out which lineage a person belongs to.
questions.s: Èrí tí a fi ń mọ ọmọ deledele ni ...?

questions.e: A narrative poem (ewì oníròyìn) tells a story in verse, so it serves as storytelling. Ìjìnlẹ̀ and àlàyé are not story-telling genres.
questions.s: Èsẹ̀ tí o wulo gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìtàn èdè ni ...?

questions.e: Religion and culture are interpreted and made clear through explanation (àlàyé), which spells out their meaning and importance. This tests knowing what àlàyé is used for.
questions.s: Èsìn àti àșà se e túmọ̀ nínú ...?

questions.e: Oríkì is praise poetry that extols a person, their lineage or their deeds, so it means praising someone (ìyìn ẹni), not news or general knowledge.
questions.s: Oríkì jé ...?

questions.e: Ìjálá chants praise brave hunters, heroes and notable figures, so praise of the valiant (ìyìn akíkanjú) is its typical content. It is not a play song or ritual story.
questions.s: Kí ni àpẹẹrẹ ìjálá?

questions.e: Alárìnjó were travelling Yoruba masquerade theatre troupes whose performances combined drama with song and dance, not dance or poetry alone.
questions.s: Alárìnjó máa ń ṣe ...?

questions.e: Oríkì is praise of a person (ìyìn ẹni), recalling their qualities, lineage and achievements. It is not pleading, accusation or a picture story.
questions.s: Oríkì jé ...?

questions.e: Farmers sing work songs (orin iṣẹ́) to keep rhythm and lift their spirits while working. Ìjálá belongs to hunters, not farmers.
questions.s: Irú orin tí àwọn agbẹ maa ń kọ́ ni ...?

questions.e: Using an animal or other object to stand for an idea or person is symbolism or illustration (àpẹẹrẹ), a common device in Yoruba proverbs and tales.
questions.s: Kínni orúkọ fífi ohun bí ẹranko ṣàpẹẹrẹ?

questions.e: "Yọjú" means to show up or appear (fara hàn), as when someone suddenly turns up somewhere. It does not literally mean "see a face" or "walk".
questions.s: Kí ni ìtumọ̀ “yọjú"?

questions.e: This tests types of Yoruba names. An orúkọ àtọ̀runwá/àtọkànwá type name is a special name tied to a person or the circumstances of birth, unlike nicknames or insulting names.
questions.s: Kí ni orúkọ tí a kọ́ mọ́ ibi tàbí ẹni kan?

questions.e: This item tests prose genres. Àròsọ is imaginative prose fiction (a story), unlike drama (eré), explanation (àlàyé) or praise poetry (oríkì).
questions.s: Kí ni apẹẹrẹ ìtàn aláwọ̀pupa?

questions.e: The sentence "Ẹ má ṣe jẹ́ kí ẹ̀mí yín lẹ" tells listeners what to do (do not lose heart), so it is a piece of advice, ìmọ̀ràn, not an expression of sorrow or experience.
questions.s: "Ę má șe je kí ẹ̀mí yín lè” jé ...

questions.e: "Kì í ṣe òun ló jà" (it was not him who fought) rejects the accusation outright, so it shows denial. Option B confirms the accusation, while D only asks a question.
questions.s: Àyọkà tí ó ni àfihàn àìtọ́ ẹ̀sùn ni ...?
o: Kì í șe òun ló jà.
Ó dájú pé òun ló jà.
Șé o sọ pé òun ló jà?

Kí ló yẹ ká șe sí àșà gẹ́gẹ́ bí àpilẹ̀kọ?

questions.e: Before Christianity arrived, the Yoruba practised òrìṣà worship (ìjọsìn Òrìṣà), serving deities such as Ṣàngó, Ọya and Ògún.
questions.s: Èsìn Yoruba ti o șáájú Kristęni ní ...?

questions.e: "Tálákà" means a poor or needy person (aláìní). Its opposite is ọlọ́rọ̀, a rich person.
questions.s: Kí ni ìtumọ̀ "tàlàkà"?

questions.e: "Ìdàbí" expresses likeness or resemblance, meaning "as if" (bí ẹni pé), used when comparing one thing to another.
questions.s: "Ìdàbí" túmò sí ...?

questions.e: "Bí a bá dákẹ́, a máa gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ àgbà" teaches that by keeping quiet and listening, the young learn the elders' wisdom and accounts of the past.
questions.s: Owe wo ni a fi ń tọ́ka sí ìtàn ìgbàanì?
o: Àìmọ̀ ní ń jé kó dà bí àrìnrìn
Agbára ọmọdé kì í tó kàkà
Bí a bá dákẹ́, a máa gbọ́ ọ̀rò àgbà
Àgbà tí kò kàwé, kì í kó ìtàn

questions.e: A comedy (eré aláwàdà) aims at laughter and humorous chatter rather than a serious theme, unlike tragedy (eré ìbànújẹ́) or historical plays.
questions.s: Eré tí kò ní kókó, ṣùgbọ́n kún fún àròyé ati erin, ni ...?

questions.e: The proverb uses fire and wind to show that trouble cannot spread unless it is started or allowed. So if a person gives trouble no opening, none will arise.
questions.s: "Bí iná kò bá tàn, ẹ̀fúùfù ò leè mú un lọ.” Òwe yìí túmọ̀ sí pé:
o: Ọjó tí iná bá tàn, ẹ̀fúùfù ń gbẹ̀
Tí a kò bá jà, wahalà ò ní yọ
Bí ẹniyan kò bá fi àyẹ fun wahalà, kò ní șiʼwahalà
